annotation.title_clean: Liability for robots II: an economic analysis
annotation.title_en: Liability for robots II: an economic analysis
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Guerra, A.; Parisi, F.; Pi, D.
annotation.summary_en: Economic-analysis paper proposing a 'manufacturer residual liability' rule for robot accidents: operators and victims are liable if negligent, and manufacturers are residually strictly liable for non-negligent accidents. A formal model shows this rule yields efficient care, activity levels, safety R&D and adoption of safer robots.
key_provisions_or_claims: Proposes manufacturer residual liability (MRL) for robots operated with human intervention.
Operators and victims bear liability for negligence; manufacturers bear residual strict liability for non-negligent accidents.
MRL incentivizes efficient care, activity levels, safety R&D and adoption of safer robots.
Damages go to faultless victims rather than the state, unlike Shavell's decoupling proposal.
Existing negligence and products liability rules inadequately address robot accident incentives.
